gloss: lost item; something one has lost

definitions.gloss: lost item; something one has lost
definitions.explanation: An item the owner has misplaced and whose whereabouts are unknown. Compare with {落|お}とし{物|もの} (a dropped item, typically found by someone else).

examples.japanese: {失|な}くし{物|もの}が{見|み}つかった。
{鍵|かぎ}や{財布|さいふ}など、{失|な}くし{物|もの}が{多|おお}くて{困|こま}っている。
examples.english: I've been losing a lot of things lately — keys, wallets — and it's becoming a problem.

notes:
Compound of {失|な}くす (to lose) + {物|もの} (thing). The connecting い of the verb stem is dropped.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {失|な}くし{物|もの}をする: to lose something
- {失|な}くし{物|もの}が{見|み}つかる: a lost item is found
- {失|な}くし{物|もの}{防止|ぼうし}タグ: lost-item prevention tag (e.g., AirTag)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {落|お}とし{物|もの}: a dropped/found item — emphasis on having been dropped, often found and turned in by others. Lost-and-found offices are {落|お}とし{物|もの}{係|がかり}, not {失|な}くし{物|もの}{係|がかり}.
- {忘|わす}れ{物|もの}: a forgotten item — left behind somewhere (in a store, on a train); the owner usually knows where they left it.
